q: Rubisco can also react with O2 instead of CO2. When is this most likely, and why is it wasteful?
options: In cool, dark conditions – O2 reacts with Rubisco to produce extra glucose overnight
In hot, dry, bright conditions when stomata close – RuBP is wasted and fixed CO2 is lost
At high CO2 levels – Rubisco becomes fully saturated with CO2 and switches over to using O2
At night – Rubisco reacts with O2 to make ATP, which then competes with the light reactions
explanation: Rubisco's active site can't fully tell CO2 from O2. When stomata close to save water, CO2 inside the leaf falls and O2 from photosynthesis builds up; heat also favours the oxygenase reaction. RuBP + O2 gives one GP plus a 2C compound that must be recycled at an energy cost, releasing CO2 (photorespiration). C4 and CAM plants concentrate CO2 around Rubisco to reduce this.
